surfaces.part: top band of the booth header

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a 30-wide rectangle on rows 0-29. Rows 1-3 form a light pink band at the top, and row 4 is a white line that works as a front-edge line. Rows 5-6 are darker pink and work as eave shadow. Below that is a vertical front face: the header with window highlights on rows 7-12, a grey ledge line on row 13, then the striped curtain and the screen panel down to row 28. The top band is thin and the whole drawing is mostly a flat front view, so this is a borderline case, but a banded top with an edge line and shadow is present, followed by a front face of more than 15 rows.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a pink booth with a lighter sign band, a striped or ribbed body and a side panel with a small screen. It has about 4 pink steps, from a light highlight through mid pinks to a dark rose edge. Its outlines are a tinted dark rose, not neutral black, and the measured near-neutral share of dark edge pixels is 0%. Vertical ribbing and the panel details break up the surfaces, so there are no flat fills (near-flat coverage 0%). It shows 15 visible tones per tile, close to the cheese stall (17) and the well (20) and above the hedge (9). Its 20 total colours are fewer than the 38-40 of the richest references, and its texture is less grainy than their tile scallops and stone shading. That makes it slightly lower by eye, but a careful artist would still accept it next to the references and it does not look like a sticker.

surfaces.part: front face with sign lights, curtain and monitor panel

answer.evidence: The column scan shows a lightening pink band at rows 1-3 that ends in a white front-edge line at row 4. Rows 5-6 below it are darker pink, which reads as eave shadow. That gives a top surface about 4 rows tall. Below it the front face runs from row 5 to row 28 (about 24 rows): sign lights at rows 7-12, a grey ledge line at row 13, a striped curtain, and a white monitor panel on the right. No receding side face is drawn. The top band is thin and could also be read as a cornice strip, so this is a borderline call, but it has both an edge line and shadow.
